source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Radiator and Grille, p.13-2

procedures.title: Aluminum radiator (Corvette): remove and install
steps: Raise the hood and drain the radiator; for safety, put a bolt in the hole of the hood support bracket.
Disconnect the radiator inlet and outlet hoses and the supply tank hose at the radiator.
Remove the shroud-to-radiator support bracket screws (the L88 427 has no fan shroud).
Remove the shroud-to-radiator baffle bracket screws and let the shroud rest on the fan.
Remove the radiator upper support bracket screws and lift the radiator out carefully.
Installation: install in reverse order (see figure 5 in the manual for the assembled position), refill the cooling system and check for leaks.

procedures.title: Copper radiator (Corvette): remove and install
steps: Raise the hood and drain the radiator; for safety, put a bolt in the hole of the hood support bracket.
Disconnect the radiator inlet and outlet hoses, and the transmission cooler lines if fitted.
Remove the shroud-to-radiator support bracket screws, then the shroud-to-baffle bracket (or radiator support) screws, and let the shroud rest on the fan.
Remove the upper support bracket screws, take off the brackets and insulators, and lift the radiator out carefully.
Installation: install in reverse order (see figure 5 in the manual), refill the cooling system and check for leaks.

procedures.title: Engine fan shroud: replace
steps: Usually the engine fan must come off first to get clearance to remove the shroud.
